What it is. Investor accounts open at the two depositories, NSDL and CDSL, at month end.

How to read it. A count of accounts, not of people: one investor can hold several. It only grows, so compare it with its own pace, not its record.

items.title: September demat additions fall 11.5% to 2.89 million after August's surge
items.author: Shilpa Rangarajan
items.text:
September's new demat account additions slowed by 11.5 per cent to 2.89 million, moderating August’s boom, with monthly additions similar to July’s.

The slowdown ended a five-month rally of rising additions that began after March, when 2.15 million accounts were opened, the lowest in a year. The additions took the total number of demat accounts to 240.6 million, according to data from depositories NSDL and CDSL. August had seen 3.27 million accounts opened, the highest in seven months, after January's 3.72 million.

...

Compared with a year ago, additions were up 17.6 per cent from the 2.46 million accounts opened in September 2025. The total account base has grown 16.2 per cent over the same period. The monthly additions remain well below the peak of 4.79 million recorded in September 2024.

...

For the July–September quarter, 9.04 million accounts were added, up 28.6 per cent from 7.03 million in April–June and 14.2 per cent from 7.92 million a year ago. This was the highest quarterly tally since October–December 2024, when 9.88 million accounts were added.

...

## ... caps

...

CDSL continued to account for the bulk of new accounts. It added 2.41 million in September, against 0.48 million at NSDL, and now holds 193.4 million accounts, or about 80 per cent of the total.

items.text:
## Demat Account Growth and CDSL Market Share vs NSDL

India’s demat ecosystem has expanded. CDSL ended March 2026 with about 18.01 crore beneficial owner accounts, up from 15.30 crore a year earlier. IBEF reported that, by July 2026, CDSL had 18.83 crore accounts and NSDL about 4.62 crore active client accounts; the combined number was roughly 23.44 crore. Keep in mind the differences in the counting definitions and rounding.

| Depository (July 2026) | Demat Accounts |
| --- | --- |
| CDSL | 18.83 crore (~80.3%) |
| NSDL | 4.62 crore (~19.7%) |

(Source: IBEF investment overview, August 2026; CDSL FY26 annual report)

CDSL’s approximate 80% share relates to account numbers, not securities held in custody by value. NSDL holds a position in institutional custody and settlement. Demat accounts can also include dormant and multiple accounts, so the headline total does not represent the same number of active individual investors.

items.title: CDSL shares gain as IPO boom pushes new demat account additions to seven-month high
items.author: Varun Yadav
items.text:
At the end of August, the total number of demat accounts in India stood at around 23.7 crore.

Central Depository Services Limited (CDSL) shares rose 2 per cent on Monday, as new demat account openings hit a seven-month high in August 2026 ... This is the third consecutive month where investors base has expanded due to rising primary market activity and upcoming IPO ... .

...

According to Zee Business research data, a total of 32.7 lakh new demat accounts were added in August, the highest monthly addition since January, when 36.2 lakh accounts were opened.

...

At the end of August, the total number of demat accounts in India stood at around 23.7 crore.

...

| Month | New Demat Accounts Added (Lakh) |
| --- | --- |
| January | 36.2 |
| February | 28.1 |
| March | 21.5 |
| April | 22.9 |
| May | 21.7 |
| June | 25.7 |
| July | 28.9 |
| August | 32.7 |

...

## CDSL is the leader in the category

CDSL continued to account for the bulk of new demat account additions in August, adding 27.4 lakh accounts during the month. NSDL, meanwhile, added 5.3 lakh accounts.

As a result, CDSL's share of the demat account market increased to 83.85 per cent in August from 81.01 per cent in the previous month.

Market participants expect the pace of account additions to remain firm in the coming months, supported by the growing participation of retail investors and the strong primary market pipeline.

According to Equirus, revenue from the Myboard IPO rose 36 per cent, highlighting the increasing activity in the IPO market.

The continued rise in demat accounts reflects the broader expansion of India's retail investor base, with more individuals gaining access to equities through digital investment platforms.
